fragments.text: I think undertagging of old turns is laziness.

reply_text:
㊥ Gist: You are right, and I take back my acceptance of chunk 1. Its readers never looked at a single Baldwin pattern, and my measurements show the same fault across all earlier readings, the live ones included.

🈹 (my "the library may have little on them") That was wrong and I had not checked it. The library has 29 patterns that mention Baldwin, including a `baldwin/` family of 11. The reading of your Baldwin turn looked at three patterns and none of them was one of those.

㊩ (why it happened) The readers search for the move and drop the subject. Their queries for that turn were "shift the work from running experiments to building the argument" and "point out that a pattern library for the concept is missing". Neither contains the word Baldwin. When I ran a query with the word in it, the search tool returned `baldwin/ARGUMENT`, `baldwin/two-claims-not-one` and `meta/baldwin-ratchet-defeats-darkroom` as its top three.

㊢ (how widespread it is) I counted turns that name a pattern family outright and where the reader read no pattern from that family:

| Readings | Turns naming a family | No pattern of that family read |
|---|---|---|
| Batches | 492 of 3,783 | 441 |
| Live | 91 of 934 | 83 |

The most common misses are `war-machine` (152 turns), `cascades` (81) and `inbox-zero` (66). So this is a fault in the instruction, not in one reader. Family names such as `features` and `control` are also ordinary words, so some of those counts overstate it. `war-machine` and `inbox-zero` are not ambiguous.

🈕 (a detail on that turn) Your turn says "there is no `futon3/library/baldwin/`". The family's first pattern was added the same day, and another on 14 August. So that turn is the origin of the family, which is a stronger relation than a citation. Two Baldwin patterns already existed at the time and were also unread: `futon-theory/baldwin-cycle` from February and `problems/baldwin-causal-claims-vs-engineering-metaphor` from March.

㊭ (changes to the reading instruction)
1. Two searches per fragment: one for the move and one for the subject, the latter using the turn's own nouns.
2. When the turn names a pattern family, the reader reads that family's patterns and cites or rejects them explicitly.
3. The checker fails a reading where a named family has no pattern read. I have that check written as `/tmp/claude17/subject_check.py`. Its wider form, which looks at any rare title word, is too noisy to use as a gate, and the family-name form is the usable one.
4. A pattern that did not exist when the turn was written can still be cited, with a note that the turn came first.

🈸 (two decisions)
- Shall I apply changes 1 to 4 to the backfill packet and the live 象 instruction together? The live change raises the interpretation version.
- The 441 batch readings and 83 live ones that missed a named family could be reread for patterns only, keeping their segments and intents. Do you want that queued after the backfill, or before it?

㊢ (in flight) Chunk 2 on 象-sonnet went out under the old instruction. I will judge it with the new check when it returns and expect it to show the same fault.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: Gist: Yes, let's revise the annotator. A session backlog follows directly from the wiring, and I have dispatched the first piece: a parser that gives each paragraph of an agent reply an id.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(revising the 象 annotator) The revision is small, because 象 already gets a note of what the agent said when it reads your turn. The instruction would change in two ways:
- The request lists the previous reply's paragraphs with their ids, marks and targets.
- For each fragment of your turn, 象 records which of those paragraphs it answers, or none.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (the session backlog) With that field, the backlog needs no further judgement from 象. It is every agent paragraph of a kind that expects a response, such as a request, a proposal or a reported problem, that no fragment of yours has answered. An item leaves the backlog when you answer it, or when the agent retracts or supersedes it. This is the operator-facing half of the commitments ledger already on the interactive list: what has been put to you and is still open.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(what `!unfinished` would show now, compiled by hand from this session) These are things I put to you that have no answer yet:
- A supersede option for the publisher, so that readers can correct their own readings.
- A mapping for the 3,626 fragments with off-list labels in the older batches.
- Whether retractions of one seed set count as separate votes in the War Machine's selection.
- Whether to give consecutive-turn links their earlier-to-later direction.
- The authored `@how` links for the gap, assertion and closing patterns.
- The one-key vote between the embedding's pattern and 象's patterns.
- Putting fragment ids in the turn header at send time.
- The stuck prompt card, which is still showing on every turn.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (`!` commands routed to the system) Agreed. Your REPL already intercepts `undo` and `yes` before they reach the agent, so there is a place for this. `!unfinished` would print the backlog without spending a turn. `!rule`, from the interactive list, belongs to the same family.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(order of work)
1. The reply parser: running now on zai-1, job `invoke-1790785459698-29232-901a9b8f`, park `park-498d0f4a-a9b0-478f-b33d-3d4952fa79d7`.
2. Record the parsed reply beside each turn record.
3. Revise the 象 instruction and validator with the "answers" field, and raise the interpretation version.
4. The backlog computation and `!unfinished`.
5. Show the wiring in the stepper: for each frame, your fragments, the paragraphs they answer, and what is left open.
